function.name: search_in_local_search_engine
function.description: Search the local search engine for pages matching the query. Each result contains the page id (page_id), a highlight-based snippet generated by the search engine, and, when available, the title. Use open_local_page_from_page_id on a promising page_id to read more of the page, or find_keyword_in_local_page_from_page_id to locate an exact phrase within it. Queries should use the most distinctive keywords for the question. Each result also carries ref, an integer citation number that is unique within this conversation and stable across searches; cite refs in the final answer.

query.description: Concise search query using the most distinctive keywords for the question.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return. Defaults to 10.

function.name: open_local_page_from_page_id
function.description: Read the text content of a page from the local search engine by its page_id. Returns a dict with content (the first at most max_chars characters of the page after cleanup, or None if the page is not found) and arguments (the call arguments). Use find_keyword_in_local_page_from_page_id when you only need to locate specific passages within a large page. The result also carries the ref assigned to this page by search; cite that ref in the final answer.

page_id.description: Exact page id returned in the results of search_in_local_search_engine.

max_chars.description: Maximum number of characters to return from the beginning of the page. Defaults to 32000.

function.name: find_keyword_in_local_page_from_page_id
function.description: Find an exact keyword or phrase in a page from the local search engine by its page_id. Returns normalized_keyword (the whitespace-normalized search term), match_count (the total number of matches found in the entire page — not limited by max_matches), matches (a list of at most max_matches context phrase strings starting from the given offset), and arguments (the call arguments). Each phrase spans diameter/2 characters before and diameter/2 characters after the matched keyword, bounded by the text edges. Use offset and max_matches to paginate through all matches when a page contains many. Use this instead of open_local_page_from_page_id when you only need to locate specific information in a large page. The result also carries the ref assigned to this page by search; cite that ref in the final answer.

page_id.description: Exact page id returned in the results of search_in_local_search_engine.

keyword.description: Exact keyword or phrase to search for. Matching is case-insensitive.

diameter.description: Total number of characters of context around each match. Half is taken before the match and half after. Defaults to 100.

max_matches.description: Maximum number of matching phrases to return in matches. Defaults to 20.

offset.description: Zero-based index of the first match to return. Use this to paginate through matches when match_count exceeds max_matches. Defaults to 0.
